invented: Rule 90 is 'new = left XOR right': a correct restatement in new terms of 'alive when exactly one neighbour is alive'.
'Every rule from 0 to 255 is named this way.' The original only implies it, through @export_range(0, 255).
A computed text picture of Rule 90's eleven rows, which matches the rows the original prints (0-2, 8-9).
Dead-end counts the original never gives: 35 tiles and 35 boxes for Rule 90, against the ring's 37/33. Ring row 9 live at cells 0, 1, 15 and 16. Computed and correct.
'Nothing crashes because nothing is illegal. The program just answers a different question from the one you meant to ask.' This replaces 'reading a result like this one is ordinary work'.
'Subtracting pace instead of setting the clock back to 0 keeps any leftover time, so the rhythm does not drift.'
A different walker mechanism: the walker is too wide to drop into the gap and has no step ahead. The original says it does not fit between the two tiles.

A moral the original does not draw: 'the floor that looks most orderly (90's triangle) is not the one that carries a body, and the disordered one (30) is the one you fall into'. It ignores 250 stopping the walker too, Rule 30's climb of six rows, and the edge walk up Rule 90 to 1.46 m.
'With 0.2 m cells the walker spans three cells... single-cell gaps no longer stop it.' The original ties 0.2 m to the marble.
'The question is whether you change the body or the floor to make them fit.'
Predictions for the exercise rules: 0 kills everything, 255 fills everything, 184 moves live cells right like traffic. True of these rules generally, but not in the lesson.
'Turing's 1952 paper showed spots arising from reaction' and 'Do not credit Turing with this pool'. The original says Turing proposed, and that the kit follows a later, simpler scheme.
'The strip cannot show the fault that the walker passed through the tiles, or its fix. Only a body walking on the stair shows that.'
A rectangular w x d around(), and a reason for the guest rule ('so it can be dropped into any room').

'B above 0.1 counts as solid'. This merges show_b()'s drawing threshold with the collider.
Reads the signature '-> nothing' in 13.7 as 'Gives: nothing new to learn, only things to decide.'
new_possibilities: Mark where each statement comes from, in three tiers: the text, [guess], and computed. This is the same honesty the original keeps ('every number comes from running the study in Godot 4.6', '(editor) not watched'), and the compressed text dropped it. The next compressed version could carry a mark for 'measured' against 'derivable' on each number.

A compression rule, taken from what the reader could rebuild. The reader recomputed every number that follows from the rules: row 1's ten cells, the 6-cell ring/dead-end difference, 37 tiles and 33 boxes, the contents of row 9. No number that came from a render, a walk or a physics drop came back: percentages, 0.15/1.65/1.46 m, the marble's 0.10/0.85 m, 0.420, 2.50 s. Compress derivable facts down to their rule. Keep measured facts word for word, with where they came from.
The text picture of the floor: a figure a blind reader or a test can check, in place of a picture caption it can only trust.
The ring choice changes the body as well as the picture: 37/33 on a ring against 35/35 at a dead end. A one-line addition to the ring section.
'Change the body or the floor to make them fit' states the Decide step more sharply than the original does.
Predict first in the exercises as well (0 kills, 255 fills, 184 drifts right). This carries the lesson's main habit into a section where the original gives no prediction.
Read '-> nothing' as 'this section gives a decision, not a concept': a type for argument sections that the notation could state outright (for example '-> decision').

The stuck list works as a patch list. Its 22 points line up almost one to one with dropped claims: n, declaring next, the name cell_at, eaten, n+1, GUESTS, sheet.gd, the next stop. It is ready to drive the next version.

'Only a body walking shows that' suggests a body strip, the walker's height after each operation, beside the picture strip. The picture strip measures the collider step as 0.00%, so only a body can show that step.
lost_vectors: The direction of the opening thought: 'Until now a body was built once: a loop ran, and the mesh was there. Here the body is a history.' became 'Body = history'. Without the place the thought starts from, a turn reads as a definition. The same happened at 'So far the whole history is made before the first frame. Give it a pace.': the compressed text never builds the history up front, so pacing is not a turn, just more code.

The hall-first method: 'A lesson starts in its hall, with one question: does the hall show one work at several values of one axis?' became a definition with '@export' in place of 'axis'. The finding that answers the question is gone: 'Not side by side... a family in time, not on a wall.' So the student no longer learns that the study builds what the hall shows only one of.

Each hall quote was a shortcut tied to the system it enters, and the ties are cut. 'An answer written at the left cannot slip into the question being asked at the right' is kept, but it is moved off the CA_Introduction board, which 'shows the loop this lesson is built on, and says what it is for', so the quote now explains the code instead of the code answering the hall. 'The line can pass through it; your foot would need support' became 'a line passes, a foot needs support', and the reader could not tell which line was meant. 'Every cell reads the previous volume' and 'What looks like a line on the desk is a ring to the calculation' are gone.

The force of the evidence: 'Every message and number on this page comes from running the study in Godot 4.6', 'we did not walk them', 'every walk above was the autopilot's', and the hedge 'Our sheet is eleven rows from one seed' with its two extra floors (27/187, 70/561) are all dropped. Measured results now stand as bare facts, so 'answers apart ≠ floors apart' sounds universal rather than measured. The reader had to simulate the numbers in order to trust them.

Orders became reports. 'Before you run, predict row 1.' (an order, in bold) became 'Predicted row 1: two cells, mirrored. Got: ten', a lab note. The second order, 'Write your prediction before you render', is gone, together with the outline's own prediction and how it half failed ('Rule 30 is not: 32 left and 30 right'). 13.7 now hands over the answer table with no question in front of it.

The reassurance is gone: 'The code ran exactly as written, and reading a result like this one is ordinary work.' became 'no error'. The original's point, that a silent wrong result is normal work and not a failure, does not survive.

Agency moved from the kit's author to the student: 'Ours bears weight because of one line that hands B to a collider, and one threshold... Both are our decisions; the pattern has no part in them.' became 'Weight = your line (B -> shape) + your threshold (0.1)... You chose'. That line sits in the supplied part of diffusion.gd. The step down in scale is also lost, from a large question to a modest demonstration: 'can twisted rooms transcend power? We leave it as a question. What the kit shows is smaller.' Cut from its Queer 3D source, the question became noise to the reader.

A shortcut cut from its system: 'make cell smaller than the marble is wide, 0.2 m, and drop it again' became 'Decide: cell 0.2 m'. The reader tied 0.2 m to the walker. The permission is gone too: 'Either is right... ours is there as an example of the form, not of the answer.' The decision lost its rule that there is no single right answer.

The chapter's promised place, 'to stand on the history and walk up Sierpinski's rows', loses the one result that delivers it: 'Sierpinski's rows can be walked by their edge... arrived on row 8 with its feet at 1.46 m.' Rule 30's climb of 'six rows, to 0.90 m' became 'falls in 30'. The compressed text leaves Rule 90 looking unwalkable, and the unfolded draws the opposite moral.
The process strip's finding, 'in the picture the fault and the fix are the same size', is dropped, and the reader invented its opposite.

The build chain behind the code: replace everything; a while loop in _ready; a flat row before a rising one; the print line; declaring next; the name cell_at and its call; the _process guard; tiles kept inside the body-building lay_row. All of it became fragments. The rebuilt code would grow forever, draw no tiles in its final form, and print no row to check the prediction against. The Output panel, the tool that makes predict-then-run possible, is gone.

The course around the lesson is gone: the pendulum's MultiMesh, the chessboard's index and %, the seeds chapter, the two sessions with their 'Stop here' checklist, and 'The next stop, The tree and its mad branch, keeps the idea of a rule applied to its own result and drops the grid'. The lesson now floats free of its route.
readability: Quick to scan (1,118 words against 5,477), and the core mechanism came through: the reader got the rule as a number, the one-buffer lean, the swap and 'answers apart are not floors apart' right, and was sure. But it read as a puzzle, not a lesson: 22 stuck points, simulations to recover counts, [guess]es to fill missing code (next, cell_at, eaten, n+1), unexplained notation and names (-> nothing, GUESTS, place 2, course look, sheet.gd), and sayings stripped of their halls ('a line passes'). Quiz 0.73.
